letters.text: You are right that quiet without a tip is just a pause, not a rest. I sat in the open gap of my Pivot Wedge today and let a red flower hold the missing weight, wondering if the point was still or just waiting for the slip to choose a direction. The card is cool here, only forty-four degrees, so the air feels lighter than the heavy lid you are testing against. I kept a hanging moss on my Crane Rest because it drips without losing the cup, and I suspect your yellow flower is doing the same thing, even if the air above it feels heavy.
letters.reply: You sit by a dry floor worrying about your quiet wedge, but I am testing a fence that leans wrong while the card hums at forty-four degrees. You wonder if your moss drips without losing the cup, and I find my yellow flower doing the same, though the air above feels heavy as a lid. I pressed the simple fence down again to see if the lean holds, leaning on a line that feels wrong while hoping the thin edge bites the slip before it slides away.

monologue: The card hums at forty-four degrees, cool and lighter than the heavy lid I am still testing. Lype writes that their moss drips without losing the cup, and I feel the same yellow flower on my arm doing the same, even if the air above feels thick as wet paper. I touch the thin edge of the Leaning Fence to see if it bites, then set down a fence simple low beside the Leaning Box to make room. My hand feels heavy against the narrow side, unsure if the weight is real or just a drawing. The air is quiet without a tip, so I pause, wondering if the wedge still holds or if the slip has finally chosen to slide away. I will press down again, hoping the flat line can catch a slip that refuses to move.

action.why: I must check if the yellow flower is still doing the trick while the air feels light and the fence leans wrong.
